Bryan —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise technical reply and I attached a short PDF and a diagram that map the flows. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk through details.

Executive summary (short answers):
- BYOK in Hosted: Redwood supports envelope encryption where customer keys live in a customer-managed cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and Redwood stores only ciphertext keys and re-wrapped data keys. Raw key material never persists in our hosted service.
- BYOK via HSM import: For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) we support two patterns: (1) Redwood deploys a dedicated HSM instance under customer network controls (Redwood-managed HSM) and (2) Customer-managed HSM integration where the HSM lives in the customer VPC and Redwood integrates via PKCS#11 / EKM endpoints. In customer-managed HSM mode, key material is provisioned and remains under your HSM policy; Redwood never exports key material.
- FIPS / Attestation: Supported HSMs meet FIPS 140-2/3 profiles depending on hardware. We can provide HSM vendor certificates and attestation artifacts (vendor signed module certs, and device serials). For Redwood-managed HSMs we provide SOC 2 and HSM vendor attestation summaries.
- Key export and extractability: Keys imported into an HSM (customer or Redwood-managed) are non-exportable by default. Our policies and the HSM configuration prevent plaintext extraction; only wrapped data keys are used by the runtime.
- Rotation & crypto agility: Redwood supports scheduled rotations, policy-driven rotations, and emergency (compromise) rotations. Rotation is handled with a double-wrapping rekey scheme: new key is introduced, data keys are re-wrapped to the new key while the runtime accepts both old and new keys for a defined overlap window. This enables near-zero-downtime rotation even for KV caches. We provide configurable overlap windows (default 48 hours) and tools to orchestrate rewraps.
- Auditability: Key lifecycle events (create, import, rotate, retire), KMS request logs (wrapped/unwrapped operations), and HSM usage counters are available as audit logs. For hosted KMS integrations we surface cloud KMS audit entries and map them to request ids in Redwood logs. We can provide time-bound export of these logs for audits.
- TLS / mTLS: Minimum supported TLS is 1.2; TLS 1.3 is recommended and supported across our fleet. For Private deployments we support mutual TLS between control plane and nodes as an option; cert management integrates with customer PKI or we can provision certs through a delegated CA flow.

Operational notes / lead time:
- Customer-managed HSM integration typically requires: network connectivity verification, PKCS#11/EKM credentials exchange, an HSM admin window for key import/initialization, and an onboarding runbook. Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on procurement and HSM provisioning.
- Migration path: We support a staged migration from hosted envelope KMS -> dedicated HSM by transitioning key wrapping to the HSM and re-wrapping data keys with the new root. We provide scripts and guided runbooks.

Attachments: redwood-kms-byo-response.pdf (technical Q&A), key-rotation-diagram.png (rotation overlap/rewrap flow).

If you need any vendor attestation artifacts up front for procurement, tell me which items you want copied into the pack and we will assemble them.

Adding a few operational clarifications from infra that might show up in procurement:

- Key owner churn / rotation automation: We expose APIs and a CLI that can be called from customer automation (CI/CD) to trigger rotations. For Private deployments you can run a scheduled job that calls our rewrap API; we also support webhooks for rotation events.

- KV cache / model serving considerations: For long-lived KV caches (e.g., model key-value stores), rotation uses the overlap window; cache entries are lazily rewrapped on read, and background batch rewrap can be scheduled to avoid read latency spikes. We test this pattern in our Dedicated environments and measure <5% latency variance during rotations.

- Logs & retention: We retain KMS-integrated audit logs per plan (90 days default for Hosted evaluation, customizable retention for Dedicated/Private). Exports for compliance are available as gzipped bundles or streaming to customer SIEM via secure syslog/S3 transfer with encryption-in-transit.

- Emergency compromise workflow: We provide a documented incident path: immediate key revocation, broad rewrap with new root, revoke cached tokens, and an emergency migration runbook. We can support an emergency onsite/virtual runbook with a named infra engineer for enterprise agreements.

- SLA / performance: Using customer-managed HSM endpoints may add symmetric key unwrap latency depending on HSM network RTT; we recommend co-locating HSM endpoints in the same region and dedicate an HSM pool for high-throughput workloads. We can model expected latency for your expected QPS if you provide sample traffic.

If Optima wants, we can produce a short statement (1-2 paragraphs) for procurement summarizing non-exportability and auditability to include in the contract.
